work_completed: Investigated 'Sign-in failed, or this Vercel account is not allowed' on nlt-pi-mvp.vercel.app. Evidence: all five sign-in variables present in Production; VERCEL_APP_REDIRECT_URI is https://nlt-pi-mvp.vercel.app/api/auth/callback; runtime logs show GET /api/auth/callback reached on production at 19:55 and 20:05 UTC; login did not return 503, so the app is configured. That narrows the cause to bad_request, exchange_failed or not_allowed.

At the owner's request, changed NLT_OWNER_VERCEL_SUBS to 'yQOE2lMYO9r9PYTGvZjxRj2D,jdub1216' (Vercel MCP) and, at the owner's request, redeployed production (dpl_DL1FxEeKheWLG1SjH2iYddE47f4q, same commit 266e533). The owner reports the same error; the 20:05 callback ran on the new deployment, so the allow-list id alone was not the cause.

Added a server-side failure line to the callback: finishLogin returns a `detail` with each failure (Vercel's `error` query parameter, state cookie missing/expired, code missing, state mismatch, token/userinfo HTTP status and OAuth `error` code, or for not_allowed the sub and username Vercel returned). handlers.callback writes `nlt-signin: failed reason=<reason> <detail>` via deps.log (default console.warn). The browser outcome is unchanged (/?signin=failed). Values from Vercel are reduced to [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] and 64 characters; no code, token, secret or cookie is logged (tested).
Tests: two new auth tests (eight failure paths with exact log lines and leak checks; nothing logged on success).
